build_description: MyoFLAME 1.0: 50 named muscle columns on FLAME 2020, surface line-muscle response basis, live jaw muscles through the jaw muscle law.

jaw_law.law: q_open = q_open_max * clip(mean(a_dig) - kappa_m mean(a_mas) - kappa_t mean(a_tem), 0, 1); inverse: a_dig_L = a_dig_R = clip(q_open / q_open_max, 0, 1), closers 0

muscles.name: Levator_Palpebrae_Superioris_L
muscles.note: levator palpebrae superioris: arises from the lesser wing of the sphenoid above the optic canal and runs forward over the globe; at Whitnall's ligament (superior orbit, just behind the orbital rim) it turns from horizontal to vertical and its aponeurosis inserts into the skin and tarsal plate of the upper eyelid (Standring, Gray's Anatomy 41e, ch. 41 Orbit and accessory visual apparatus; Z-Anatomy). FACS AU5 Upper Lid Raiser (Ekman, Friesen and Hager 2002). Placement on the template: target = the pretarsal upper-lid skin on the pupil column (FLAME vertex 3855, 1 mm outside the eyeball sphere, lid margin); origin = the pulley point (Whitnall's ligament) 19 mm above and 6 mm behind the eyeball centre (31.7, 21.4, 26.0), which is the effective line of action of the aponeurosis (the true origin at the orbital apex would give a medial-posterior pull that drives the lid margin into the globe); the pull is projected tangent to the eyeball at every vertex (globe_tangential) so the lid slides up over the globe; 4 mm footprint radius (8 mm sigma) so the upper lid moves and the brow and lower lid stay

muscles.name: Levator_Palpebrae_Superioris_R
muscles.note: levator palpebrae superioris: arises from the lesser wing of the sphenoid above the optic canal and runs forward over the globe; at Whitnall's ligament (superior orbit, just behind the orbital rim) it turns from horizontal to vertical and its aponeurosis inserts into the skin and tarsal plate of the upper eyelid (Standring, Gray's Anatomy 41e, ch. 41 Orbit and accessory visual apparatus; Z-Anatomy). FACS AU5 Upper Lid Raiser (Ekman, Friesen and Hager 2002). Placement on the template: target = the pretarsal upper-lid skin on the pupil column (FLAME vertex 3855, 1 mm outside the eyeball sphere, lid margin); origin = the pulley point (Whitnall's ligament) 19 mm above and 6 mm behind the eyeball centre (31.7, 21.4, 26.0), which is the effective line of action of the aponeurosis (the true origin at the orbital apex would give a medial-posterior pull that drives the lid margin into the globe); the pull is projected tangent to the eyeball at every vertex (globe_tangential) so the lid slides up over the globe; 4 mm footprint radius (8 mm sigma) so the upper lid moves and the brow and lower lid stay

muscles.name: Platysma_L
muscles.note: platysma: a broad sheet arising from the fascia over the upper parts of pectoralis major and deltoid, crossing the clavicle and the neck; its anterior fibres interlace below the chin, the posterior fibres cross the mandible to insert into its lower border, the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the lower face, the modiolus and the lower lip (Standring, Gray's Anatomy 41e, ch. 29 Neck; Gray 1918 sect. 4). FACS AU20 Lip Stretcher (risorius with platysma) and AU21 Neck Tightener (platysma). Placement on the template: target = skin over the mandibular body inferolateral to the modiolus (mandibular/labial part); origin = the lower border of the FLAME neck below the clavicle line (the template ends at y = -170 mm); 14 mm footprint, decaying along the neck towards the origin
